the presence of a iodine atom in the molecule of IMPPA accentuates the inhibition by IMPPA of the activation of fatty acids by CoA SH.
the presence of a para-iodine group in the molecule of IMPPA accentuates the inhibition by the myocardium of the activation of IMPPA, resulting in a high myocardial retention of IMPPA.

1) IMPPA is a long chain fatty acid analogue that accumulates in the myocardium; 2) IMPPA accumulates in the heart due to inhibition of its activation by coenzyme A; 3) the presence of an iodine atom in the molecule of the compound increases the inhibition of its activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the metabolism of 15-phenyl pentadecanoate and its derivatives, in particular, the effect of the presence of an iodine group in the molecule, on myocardial metabolism.
the development of new tracers for myocardial metabolism.
the study of a new myocardial imaging agent, IMPPA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IMPPA, which has been used for myocardial imaging, accumulates mainly in the form of unbound free fatty acids in the myocardium and that the presence of an iodine atom in the molecule is responsible for its low rate of metabolism.
the presence of the iodine group in IMPPA is responsible for the retention of myocardial radioactivity.
IMPPA is retained in the heart by inhibition of its activation by coenzyme A SH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iodine is a strong inhibitor of IMPPA-CoA activation, which results in a high retention of myocardial IMPPA activity.
the retention of myocardial 14C activity following injection of IMPPA is due to the accumulation of unmetabolized IMPPA following the inhibition of activation.
iodine-containing IMPPA is a useful myocardial imaging agent, but the presence of iodinated IMPPA in myocardial cells does not necessarily indicate that it is metabolized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a iodine in the IMPPA molecule strongly reduces its metabolic rate, which is responsible for its accumulation in the myocardium.
the iodine atom present in IMPPA inhibits the activation of IMPPA by CoA SH.
the presence of a halogen in the molecule of fatty acids can lead to an accumulation of free fatty acid in the myocardium.
